// about: The argument schema of mission scripts (milestone M6a). Facts in plain words. Evidence names the record of the fact (a TR rule, a GA1 row or an MSD section of the mission studio design) and the fork class, when the fork has the behavior. The help texts follow the STE rules of AGENTS.md.

slotNotes.baseEntry: The game code saves this mission only after the first landing on its start base. At that landing, the code applies the mission state again.
slotNotes.joinAtBase: The game code joins this mission at the first base landing. Then it reports the accept and starts the first base scene of the mission.
slotNotes.shipBuy: A ship buy at a story stage from 15 to 22 changes the attitude of the player to one faction. The game code sets the attitude to -0.2.
slotNotes.acceptReputation: The accept of this mission sets the same attitude to -0.2, also when the player buys no ship.
slotNotes.storyEnd: The game code shows its own end text after the success. Then the story stays at its last stage.

help.title: Start other triggers
help.whatItIs: Starts other triggers. The game starts them after all actions of this trigger.

help.title: Stop other triggers
help.whatItIs: Stops other triggers, so that they do not run.

help.title: Checkpoint
help.whatItIs: Saves the game at this point. After a load, the mission continues at the trigger that the line names.

help.title: Mission end
help.whatItIs: Ends the mission with success or fail. A success moves the story to the next stage. A fail shows a text to the player.

help.title: Spawn and move
help.whatItIs: Puts ships, formations, solars and loot into space. Moves or removes them.
help.whatItWrites: Act_SpawnShip, Act_SpawnFormation, Act_SpawnSolar, Act_SpawnLoot, Act_Destroy and related lines.

help.title: Orders
help.whatItIs: Tells ships what to do: fly to points, follow, stay near or dock.
help.whatItWrites: Act_GiveObjList lines that name an [ObjList] section.

help.title: Sides
help.whatItIs: Sets who is friendly and who is hostile. Ships fight when their attitude is hostile and they are near.

help.title: Plot armor and marks
help.whatItIs: Protects ships, changes their hull, marks them on the screen or cloaks them.
help.whatItWrites: Act_Invulnerable, Act_AdjHealth, Act_MarkObj, Act_Cloak and Act_LightFuse lines.

help.title: Area rules
help.whatItIs: Limits the attackers and the ambient traffic during the mission.

help.title: Leave-area warnings
help.whatItIs: Plays a warning when the player leaves an area or does not come. After four warnings, the mission fails.

help.title: Comms
help.whatItIs: Plays comm lines and conversations, shows pop-ups and plays sounds.
help.whatItWrites: Act_SendComm, Act_StartDialog, Act_EtherComm and related lines.

help.title: Objectives and text
help.whatItIs: Sets the objective, its marker and route, the mission title, the offer text and the log text.
help.whatItWrites: Act_SetNNObj, Act_NNIds, Act_SetTitle and related lines.

help.title: Cutscenes and base scenes
help.whatItIs: Plays space cutscenes, sets the camera, and adds or removes scenes in bases.
help.whatItWrites: Act_CallThorn, Act_RevertCam, Act_AddRTC and related lines.

help.title: Player
help.whatItIs: Moves the player, changes the ship, the money and the cargo, and allows or locks docking and maneuvers.
help.whatItWrites: Act_MovePlayer, Act_AdjAcct, Act_PlayerCanDock and related lines.

help.title: World
help.whatItIs: Locks or unlocks docks and gates, turns off trade lanes and arms random encounters.
help.whatItWrites: Act_LockDock, Act_DisableTradelane, Act_EnableEnc and Act_DisableEnc lines.

help.title: Debug
help.whatItIs: Lines for tests. They do nothing for the player.

missionsTab.title: Missions
missionsTab.whatItIs: The list of all mission scripts in the game data and the mods. The 14 story slots come first, in the fixed order of the game code.
missionsTab.whatItWrites: Nothing. Each row opens a mission script.

missionGraph.title: Mission graph
missionGraph.whatItIs: A map of the triggers of one mission. Each box is one trigger. A line shows that one trigger starts, stops, loads or watches another trigger.
missionGraph.whatItWrites: Nothing in this version. Each box shows one [Trigger] section of the mission script.

missionItems.title: Mission items
missionItems.whatItIs: The ships, points, volumes and paths of the open mission in this system.
missionItems.whatItWrites: Nothing. The positions come from the mission script.

mission.title: Mission
mission.whatItIs: A mission script: the triggers, ships, orders, objectives and conversations of one mission. The game loads it for a story slot.
mission.whatItWrites: The mission script file, for example DATA\MISSIONS\M02\m02.ini.

storySlot.title: Story slot
storySlot.whatItIs: One of the 14 places for a story mission in the game code. The code sets the script path, the order and the start rules of each slot.
storySlot.whatItWrites: Nothing. A mod cannot change the rules of a slot. A mod can change the script of the slot.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.whatItIs: One unit of mission logic. It waits for one condition. Then it runs its actions in order.
trigger.whatItWrites: One [Trigger] section: a nickname, one Cnd_ line and the Act_ lines.

startsWhen.title: Starts when
startsWhen.whatItIs: The event that the trigger waits for. The game uses only one condition for each trigger, the last one.
startsWhen.whatItWrites: One Cnd_ line in the [Trigger] section.

act.title: Act
act.whatItIs: A part of the mission story, from one checkpoint or system to the next. The editor proposes acts. They help you read the graph.
act.whatItWrites: Nothing. A later version saves acts in an editor file of the mod. The game does not read that file.

notStarted.title: Not started by the mission
notStarted.whatItIs: The triggers that no start trigger and no checkpoint leads to. The game does not run them.
notStarted.whatItWrites: Nothing. The editor finds these triggers.

label.title: Label
label.whatItIs: One name for a group of ships, as a tag in Unity. An action on a label acts on each ship of the group.

missionShip.title: Mission ship
missionShip.whatItIs: A ship that the mission can spawn. It has three parts: the ship, the pilot and voice, and the ship build.

ship.title: Ship
ship.whatItIs: Where the ship starts, its labels, its first orders and its cargo.

pilotAndVoice.title: Pilot and voice
pilotAndVoice.whatItIs: The faction, voice, face and name of the pilot. The ship needs this part.
pilotAndVoice.whatItWrites: The [NPC] section that the ship names.

shipBuild.title: Ship build
shipBuild.whatItIs: The ship model, equipment, pilot skill and AI of the ship. The pilot and voice part needs this part.
shipBuild.whatItWrites: The [NPCShipArch] section in the mission ship file or in npcships.ini.

formation.title: Formation
formation.whatItIs: A group of ships that fly in a shape. A formation takes its ships, so they cannot spawn alone.

solar.title: Solar
solar.whatItIs: A station, a platform or another object that the mission can spawn.

loot.title: Loot
loot.whatItIs: Cargo that the mission puts into space.

orderList.title: Order list
orderList.whatItIs: A list of orders for a ship, in order: fly to a point, follow, wait or dock.

objective.title: Objective
objective.whatItIs: The objective text and marker that the player sees.

conversation.title: Conversation
conversation.whatItIs: Comm lines between speakers, in order. All speakers must be in the system of the conversation.

npc.title: NPC
npc.whatItIs: A pilot with a faction, a voice and a face. Mission ships name it.

randomEncounter.title: Random encounter
randomEncounter.whatItIs: Attackers that spawn at a time or a place while the mission arms them.

cutsceneLink.title: Cutscene link
cutsceneLink.whatItIs: The link between a trigger and a space cutscene: the cutscene file, its anchor ship and the trigger that ends it.
cutsceneLink.whatItWrites: An Act_CallThorn line and an Act_RevertCam line.

baseSceneLink.title: Base scene link
baseSceneLink.whatItIs: A scene in a base that the mission adds, for example a mission offer in a bar.
baseSceneLink.whatItWrites: Act_AddRTC and Act_RemoveRTC lines that name an RTC file.

event.title: Event
event.whatItIs: What starts a trigger, for example the player enters a system. Each trigger has one event, from its condition.

triggerComponent.title: Trigger
triggerComponent.whatItIs: When the trigger runs: with the start of the mission, and again after each run.
triggerComponent.whatItWrites: The InitState and repeatable lines of the [Trigger] section.

rawIni.title: INI
rawIni.whatItIs: The lines of the mission script as text, with the marks of the checks. The text shows the same problems as the fields.
rawIni.whatItWrites: Nothing in this version. The editor shows mission scripts but does not change them.

problems.title: Problems
problems.whatItIs: The problems that the checks find in this mission. Each problem says what the game does and how to fix it.
problems.whatItWrites: Nothing. The checks read the mission script.

openLancer.title: OpenLancer
openLancer.whatItIs: The lines that the OpenLancer engine reads but does not run. The retail game runs all lines.
openLancer.whatItWrites: Nothing. The list comes from the OpenLancer engine.

voiceLines.title: Voice lines
voiceLines.whatItIs: The comm lines that the mission plays, with the voices file of each line.
voiceLines.whatItWrites: Nothing. The comm lines are in the voices files of DATA\AUDIO.

missionText.title: Text
missionText.whatItIs: The text ids that the mission shows: titles, offers, objectives, fail texts and log lines.
missionText.whatItWrites: Nothing. The texts are in the resource files of the game.

missionFiles.title: Files
missionFiles.whatItIs: The other files of the mission: the mission ships, the base scenes, the space cutscenes and the texts.
missionFiles.whatItWrites: Nothing. Each row names files that the mission uses.

overview.title: Overview
overview.whatItIs: The counts of the parts of the mission, its systems and its start triggers.
overview.whatItWrites: Nothing. The editor counts the sections of the mission script.

behaviorPrefab.title: Behavior prefab
behaviorPrefab.whatItIs: A pattern of triggers that the mission repeats, for example a spawn wave. The editor finds the patterns and groups their triggers.
behaviorPrefab.whatItWrites: Nothing in this version. The triggers of the pattern stay as [Trigger] sections.

formationMembers.title: Members
formationMembers.whatItIs: The ships that the formation takes, in order. Each ship belongs to the formation, so it cannot spawn alone.
formationMembers.whatItWrites: The ship lines of the [MsnFormation] section.

labelMembers.title: Members
labelMembers.whatItIs: The ships, formations and solars that have this label. An action on the label acts on each of them.
labelMembers.whatItWrites: The label lines of the [MsnShip], [MsnFormation] and [MsnSolar] sections.

conversationLines.title: Lines
conversationLines.whatItIs: The comm lines of the conversation, in order: the speaker, the listener and the comm line.
conversationLines.whatItWrites: The line lines of the [Dialog] section.

prefabMembers.title: Triggers in this prefab
prefabMembers.whatItIs: The triggers of the prefab instance, each with its role in the pattern.
prefabMembers.whatItWrites: Nothing in this version. Each trigger stays a [Trigger] section.

otherSection.title: Other section
otherSection.whatItIs: A section of the mission script that has no page of its own in this version, for example [MetaBehavior] or [Constants]. The page shows its problems and its INI.
otherSection.whatItWrites: The section itself, as the INI block shows it.

keys.help: The space in meters that the ship keeps from the other ships at the spawn.

keys.label: System
keys.help: The system of the ship. The game keeps the line only when the system exists.

keys.label: Start position
keys.help: The place of the ship at the spawn.

keys.label: Placed near
keys.help: The ship starts at a heading and a range from an object, in place of a start position.

keys.label: Rotation
keys.help: The turn of the ship at the spawn, as a quaternion: W, X, Y and Z.

keys.label: Arrives through
keys.help: The object that the ship comes out of when it spawns, for example a jump gate or a base.

keys.label: Formation shape
keys.help: The shape of formations.ini. A section with this line is a formation. Put the ship keys before this line.

keys.label: Member
keys.help: An earlier [MsnShip] that the formation takes. Then the ship belongs to the formation, so it cannot spawn alone.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the lines of the mission use for the ship.

keys.label: Pilot and voice
keys.help: The [NPC] section of the pilot: the faction, the voice, the face and the ship build.

keys.label: Random pilot name
keys.help: True gives the pilot a random name.

keys.label: Labels
keys.help: Names of groups that the ship is in. A line of the mission can name a group to act on each item of it.

keys.label: Initial orders
keys.help: The order list that the ship gets at the spawn. The game keeps the first line of this key and 'Initial behavior'.

keys.label: Initial behavior
keys.help: The behavior that the ship gets at the spawn. The game keeps the first line of this key and 'Initial orders'.

keys.label: Arrives by jump
keys.help: True makes the ship follow the player through jumps. Then the ship can be in each system.

keys.label: Cargo
keys.help: A good in the hold of the ship and its count. The game skips a line with a good that it does not know.

keys.label: Hull points
keys.help: The hull points at the spawn and at a respawn. Without this line, the ship uses the hull points of its archetype.

keys.label: Spawn spacing radius
keys.help: The space in meters that the ship keeps from the other ships at the spawn.

keys.label: System
keys.help: The system of the ship. The game keeps the line only when the system exists.

keys.label: Start position
keys.help: The place of the ship at the spawn.

keys.label: Placed near
keys.help: The ship starts at a heading and a range from an object, in place of a start position.

keys.label: Rotation
keys.help: The turn of the ship at the spawn, as a quaternion: W, X, Y and Z.

keys.label: Arrives through
keys.help: The object that the ship comes out of when it spawns, for example a jump gate or a base.

keys.label: Formation shape
keys.help: The shape of formations.ini. A section with this line is a formation. Put the ship keys before this line.

keys.label: Member
keys.help: An earlier [MsnShip] that the formation takes. Then the ship belongs to the formation, so it cannot spawn alone.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the arm and disarm lines use for the encounter.

keys.label: Encounter type
keys.help: TL_Attack attacks on a trade lane. SP_Attack attacks in open space. The keys after this line belong to the encounter.

keys.label: Attacker faction
keys.help: The faction of the attackers.

keys.label: Target
keys.help: The ship that the attackers go for. Player is the ship of the player.

keys.label: Starts by
keys.help: time, then the shortest and the longest time in seconds: the attackers spawn at a time between them. location, then a point and a range: they spawn when the target comes into the range.

keys.label: Formation
keys.help: A formation that can spawn: its shape, its weight, the fewest and the most ships, then the classes of the ships with their weights.

keys.label: Form count
keys.help: The number of formations that spawn. The game picks a number from the first value to the second value.

keys.label: Labels
keys.help: Names of groups that the attackers are in. A line of the mission can name a group to act on each attacker.

keys.label: Pilot
keys.help: The pilot settings of the attackers.

keys.label: Spawn place
keys.help: The angle in degrees and the distance of the spawn from the target.

keys.label: Spawn spacing radius
keys.help: The space in meters that the game keeps free at the spawn point.

keys.label: Formation position
keys.help: A fixed place where a formation can spawn.

keys.label: Trade lane ring
keys.help: The ring of the trade lane that the attackers go for.

keys.label: Attack chance
keys.help: The chance of an attack in percent.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the objective lines use.

keys.label: Type
keys.help: How the game shows the objective: ids (a text), navmarker (a point), rep_inst (an object) or base (a base).

keys.label: State
keys.help: ACTIVE shows the objective. HIDDEN hides it until a line shows it.

keys.label: Hidden
keys.help: True hides the objective.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the triggers use for the conversation.

keys.label: System
keys.help: The system of the conversation. All speakers must be in this system.

keys.label: Line
keys.help: One comm line: the speaker, the listener and the comm line.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the ships use for this behavior.

keys.label: System
keys.help: The game does not use this value.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the order lines use for the order list.

keys.label: System
keys.help: The game does not use this value.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the other lines use for the trigger.

keys.label: Starts with the mission
keys.help: ACTIVE starts the trigger when the mission starts. The game reads the last line after the nickname.

keys.label: Repeats
keys.help: True makes the trigger active again each time it runs. The game reads the last line after the nickname.

keys.label: System
keys.help: The game does not use this value. The editor uses it to find the system of the trigger.

values.name: on
values.label: On
values.help: Only the word true turns it on. Each other word turns it off.

notes.unknownKey: The editor does not know the meaning of this key yet.
notes.ignoredCondition: The game uses only the last condition of a trigger, so it ignores this line.
notes.beforeNickname: This line comes before the nickname, so the game ignores it.
notes.missingCommLine: No voices file has this comm line. The game plays no sound for it.
notes.titleText: The title of the mission that the game code shows.
notes.missionSystems: The systems that the mission names.
notes.sharedMember: Another prefab holds this trigger. It counts for the steps of this prefab too.
notes.openCutscene: Open the space cutscene in the Cutscene tab.
notes.hullPointsNotSet: The ship uses the hull points of its archetype.

steps.name: Start trigger
steps.reason: Without a start trigger, nothing in the mission runs.

steps.name: Mission success
steps.reason: Without one success, the story cannot go to the next mission.

steps.name: Fail texts
steps.reason: The game shows this text when the mission fails.

steps.name: One condition for each trigger
steps.reason: A trigger without a condition stops the game when it starts. The game ignores all conditions but the last.

steps.name: Names resolve
steps.reason: The game ignores a name that it cannot find, so the line does nothing.

steps.name: Each trigger can start
steps.reason: The game never runs a trigger that nothing starts.

steps.name: Cutscenes end
steps.reason: Without "End camera", the camera does not come back to the player, and the player stays invulnerable.

steps.name: Pilot and voice
steps.reason: Without it, the game drops the ship.

steps.name: Ship build
steps.reason: Without it, the game drops the ship.

steps.name: Archetype, loadout and pilot
steps.reason: Without them, the game drops the ship.

steps.name: Comm lines exist
steps.reason: The game plays no sound for a missing comm line.

steps.name: Speakers in the system
steps.reason: A speaker in another system stops the conversation.

steps.name: Cutscene file
steps.reason: The game plays nothing without the file.

steps.name: Anchor
steps.reason: The camera of the cutscene moves with the anchor ship.

steps.name: Camera back
steps.reason: Without "End camera", the camera does not come back to the player.

steps.name: Scene file
steps.reason: The game plays nothing without the file.

steps.name: Path length
steps.reason: The game cuts a longer path, so it finds no file.

keys.label: Nickname
keys.help: The name that the [NPC] sections use for this ship build.

keys.label: Ship archetype
keys.help: The ship model of the build.

keys.label: Loadout
keys.help: The equipment of the ship.

keys.label: Pilot
keys.help: The pilot settings of the ship, for example how it aims and evades.

keys.label: State graph
keys.help: The set of AI behaviors of the ship, for example the set of a fighter.

keys.label: Level
keys.help: The level of the build, for example d5.

keys.label: NPC class
keys.help: The classes that encounters and missions use to pick this ship build.
